messages.author: dea7fe9fc1920d2f
messages.subject: Switch dataset in linked brush
parts:
Hi everyone,

I tried to modify the linked brush demo app to make it work with user selected data sets. After inserting a shiny selectInput (and the usual checks for empty input) it shows the graphs, but the brush doesn't work anymore. See code below. I also tried to put all data sets into one data.frame and use a ggvis input to select the data set, but this also seems to be not trivial.

Does anybody have an idea how to fix this?

Thanks a lot

Thomas



##############
# server.R

library(ggvis)

data(diamonds, package = "ggplot2")

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
revals <- reactiveValues();

output$dataset <- renderUI ({
selectInput("dataSubset", "Subset", choices = list("FirstThousand"=1, "SecondThousand" = 1000, "ThirdThausand" = 2000), selected = 1);
})
observe({
if(is.null(input$dataSubset)) {
return(NULL);
}
print(input$dataSubset);
revals$diamonds <- diamonds[as.integer(input$dataSubset):(as.integer(input$dataSubset) + 999), ];
})
lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:1000);
gv1 <- reactive({
if(is.null(revals$diamonds)) {
return(ggvis());
}
ggvis(revals$diamonds, props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +
layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8,
fill.brush := "red")) +
lb$brush_handler() +
opts(width = 300, height = 300)
})
gv2 <- reactive({
if(is.null(revals$diamonds)) {
return(ggvis());
}
ggvis(revals$diamonds, props(x = ~table, y = ~depth)) +
layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8)) +
opts(width = 300, height = 300)
})
# Set up observers for the spec and the data
observe_ggvis(gv1, "plot1", session)
observe_ggvis(gv2, "plot2", session)
})
#
############

##############
# ui.R
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
uiOutput("dataset"),
ggvis_output("plot1"),
ggvis_output("plot2")
))
#
############

messages.subject: Re: Switch dataset in linked brush
parts:
Hi Thomas,

I can get it working with a few simplifications, as shown below.
Unfortunately there seems to be a bug with non-default keys so I can't
get it working exactly right: you should be able to do set a custom
key variable so that the selection resets to zero when you show a
different subset.

Hadley

library(ggvis)
library(shiny)
data(diamonds, package = "ggplot2")

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
headerPanel("Linked brushing of subsets"),
sidebarPanel(
selectInput("dataSubset", "Subset",

choices = list("First" = 1, "Second" = 1001, "Third" = 2001))
),
mainPanel(

ggvis_output("plot1"),
ggvis_output("plot2")
)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
diamonds_subset <- reactive({
i <- as.integer(input$dataSubset)
diamonds[seq(i, i + 999), , drop = FALSE]

})

lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:1000)

gv1 <- reactive({
ggvis(diamonds_subset(), props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +

layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8,
fill.brush := "red")) +
lb$brush_handler() +
opts(width = 300, height = 300)
})

observe_ggvis(gv1, "plot1", session)

gv2 <- reactive({
ggvis(diamonds_subset(), props(x = ~table, y = ~depth)) +

layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8)) +
opts(width = 300, height = 300)
})

observe_ggvis(gv2, "plot2", session)
}

runApp(list(server = server, ui = ui))

messages.subject: Re: Switch dataset in linked brush
parts:
Thanks again, Hadley.

This brought me a huge step closer to a app to compare different data sets using the linked brush. But of course the next problem is just around the corner. The tooltip function is lost after the first switch of datasets, as discussed here last week. Example code below.

Other observations:
- linked brush for me only works in Chrome. Firefox (Linux and Windows) shows the graphs, but selects all points once you start using the brush. There is no way to select specific points.
  IE up to version 11 only shows the controls, no plot.
- the controls for the graphs are not active.


Thomas

library(ggvis)
library(shiny)
data(diamonds, package = "ggplot2")

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
headerPanel("Linked brushing of subsets with broken tooltip"),

sidebarPanel(
selectInput("dataSubset", "Subset",
choices = list("First" = 1, "Second" = 1001, "Third" = 2001))
),
mainPanel(
ggvis_output("plot1"),
ggvis_output("plot2")
)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

all_values <- function(x) {
if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")

}
diamonds_subset <- reactive({
i <- as.integer(input$dataSubset)
diamonds[seq(i, i + 999), , drop = FALSE]
})
lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:1000)
gv1 <- reactive({
ggvis(diamonds_subset(), props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +
layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8,
fill.brush := "red")) +
lb$brush_handler() +
opts(width = 300, height = 300) + tooltip(all_values)

})
observe_ggvis(gv1, "plot1", session)
gv2 <- reactive({
ggvis(diamonds_subset(), props(x = ~table, y = ~depth)) +
layer_point(props(fill := lb$fill_prop(), fillOpacity := 0.8)) +
opts(width = 300, height = 300)
})
observe_ggvis(gv2, "plot2", session)
}

runApp(list(server = server, ui = ui))
